subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & SLO fit for Stallion.ai pilot

From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@stallion.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity & SLO for Stallion.ai pilot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Stallion.ai is excited to move toward a short pilot for our real-time summarization API. A few quick context points so the sizing aligns with our product needs:

- Traffic pattern: daily warm window 08:00–20:00 PT with short hourly spikes. We also run heavy nightly analytics windows 01:00–03:00 PT.
- Target p95 latency (generation part): <= 250ms for our interactive chat endpoint.
- Peak token throughput target: up to ~6,000 tokens/sec sustained during spikes (peaks last ~10–30 minutes). Average traffic expected ~1,200 tokens/sec.
- Typical prompt lengths: median request 35–60 tokens; heavy requests up to 1,500 tokens (batch analytics).

We need a concrete recommendation for Dedicated capacity (GPUs/safe headroom) to include in our internal procurement and to size an initial committed contract. Also curious about warm/cold cache behavior, autoscaling latency, and fallback model options.

Can you share a sizing sheet and an ops runbook we can review? Ideally a 30–45 minute call with your solutions engineering + infra ops to lock down assumptions.

Thanks,
Jared
CTO, Stallion.ai

Thanks Jared — great context. High level answer first, then proposed next steps.

Quick recommendation (BOE):
- Target peak: 6,000 tokens/sec (interactive spikes) with p95 <= 250ms.
- Suggested Dedicated slab: 12 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs reserved (this gives ~2.0x headroom vs BOE).
- Canary pilot option: start with 6 GPUs for 3 weeks (to validate real-world prompt distribution & cache hit rates), then expand to reserved 12 GPUs on commit.

How I got there (summary of assumptions):
- Model family we'd expect you to run: redwood-instruct-13B-quant (optimized kernels + KV caching).
- Typical sustained per-GPU throughput (p95, interactive mix, median prompt ~45 tokens): ~1,000–1,200 tokens/sec on A100-80GB with our runtime optimizations.
- Back-of-envelope math: 6,000 tps / 1,100 tps_perGPU ≈ 5.5 -> round up to 6 GPUs baseline. Apply 2.0x headroom for tails, scheduling jitter, node failures and burst absorption -> 12 GPUs reserved.
- Nightly analytics (long-context batches) should be routed to a fallback slab (cheaper, lower-memory SKU) or run as scheduled batch jobs to avoid interfering with interactive SLOs.

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching expected to reduce per-request work for conversational flows by ~15–20% after warmup; cold-starts for large contexts can degrade throughput by ~30% until warm.
- We recommend a 3-node hot-standby pool to absorb quick spikes (warm nodes, minimal cold-start).
- Autoscale policy: keep a small buffer + rapid scale-up with pre-warmed instances; fallback to quantized 34B variant for quality-preserving but lower-throughput scenario.

Attachments: I pushed an initial sizing sheet (stallion_token_profile.csv) and a short runbook stub (stallion_runbook_v1.pdf). Link to calculation sheet is below.

Next steps:
1) 30-min technical sync with me + Irene + your infra team to validate prompt distribution and agree on pilot telemetry.
2) If agreed, we provision 6 GPU pilot for 3 weeks + instrumentation.
3) After pilot, review metrics and decide on 12 GPU reserved slab with 3 hot-standbys.

Can you do Thu 4th 10:00–10:30 PT?

—Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Adding some technical detail from an ops/runtime perspective. Quoting Karthik below for continuity.

On Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 9:35 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick recommendation (BOE):
> - Target peak: 6,000 tokens/sec ... Suggested Dedicated slab: 12 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs reserved ...

A few clarifications and recommended tuning knobs:
1) Per-GPU throughput variance by prompt length and decoding settings:
   - Median prompt (40–60 tokens), sampling temperature 0.7, greedy top-k disabled: 1,000–1,200 tokens/sec (p95).
   - Long-context generation (>= 2k tokens) drops per-GPU throughput to ~240–350 tokens/sec due to KV cache growth and memory bandwidth pressure.

2) Cache warmup and hit-rate assumptions:
   - Expect 15–25% effective token savings after 10–20 similar requests (conversational flows).
   - If your product has a high prefix reuse (session-based), we can usually reduce effective GPU need by ~1 node for the same peak.

3) Headroom math (concrete):
   - Conservative per-GPU p95: 1,000 tps.
   - Baseline GPUs = ceil(6,000 / 1,000) = 6.
   - Operational headroom: +100% (migrations, maintenance, noisy neighbors) -> reserved = 12.
   - Hot standby (3 nodes) suggested for immediate surge absorption; these count outside the reserved slab for billing/commit conversation.

4) Fallbacks & QoS policies:
   - Degrade to a smaller-but-stable model variant for non-critical requests (e.g., analytics fan-out).
   - Throttle heavy long-context batch jobs to off-peak windows or run on lower-cost on-demand pool.

Operational checklist for pilot:
- Instrumentation: token-level latency traces, KV hit-rate, GPU util, tail-latency heatmaps.
- SLIs: p95 generation latency, median latency, error rate, cache-hit fraction.
- Canary routing policy and automatic rollback thresholds.

I can share a short perf baseline script we run during the pilot that will capture per-GPU p50/p95 tokens/sec across prompt buckets. That will let us convert pilot metrics to a final commitment with confidence.

—Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
